concepts.why: The presence of an anterior mediastinal mass and mediastinal widening are highly suggestive of Hodgkin lymphoma.

contradict_spans: sinus tachycardia with low-voltage QRS and electrical alternans
concepts.why: The presence of an anterior mediastinal mass and mediastinal widening could also suggest Non-Hodgkin lymphoma, although the ECG findings are less typical.
The large pericardial effusion is consistent with pericarditis, but the presence of an anterior mediastinal mass suggests a more complex diagnosis.

support_spans: intermittent fever over the preceding 3 months
concepts.why: The combination of pericardial effusion and prolonged fever could suggest tuberculous pericarditis, but the presence of an anterior mediastinal mass is not typical.
The mediastinal widening could be consistent with sarcoidosis, but the presence of a large pericardial effusion is not typical.
The combination of an anterior mediastinal mass, large pericardial effusion, and mediastinal widening suggests lymphoma with secondary pericardial involvement.
The ECG finding of sinus tachycardia with low-voltage QRS and electrical alternans is explained by cardiac lymphoma.
